children.name: Turritella capistrata DeVries, 2018
children.description: Estimated shell length to 25 mm, pleural angle about 19 °. Protoconch unknown. Spire with about 10 whorls. Earliest preserved whorls straight-sided to concave, imbricate; spiral formula C 1 A 1 and subsequently D 2 C 1 B 2 A 1. Later whorls imbricate with strong primary spirals and insertion of secondary spirals; successive formulae D 2 C 1 t 3 B 2 s 3 A 1 r 3 and D 2 C 1 t 3 B 2 s 3 s 4 A 1 r 3 r 4; primary spiral ‘ D ’ variably exposed, primary spiral ‘ B ’ sometimes weaker than primary spirals ‘ A ’ and ‘ C ’. Spacing formula C 27 B 46 A 77 (n = 4). Lateral growth line orthocline to slightly prosocline, inflected anteriorly only. Lateral sinus moderately deep, apex situated close to spiral ‘ B ’. Base convex with at least two spirals, basal growth line probably radial, but base mostly obscured. Allmon formula 2? - 4 - S-B-OR.

children.description: Protoconch smooth, 250 µm in diameter. Transition to protoconch marked by the beginning of teleoconch sculpture. Finer cords develop from whorl four and on, below the adapical suture, between the cords and below cord three. Microsculpture consists of very fine irregularly spaced threads between all cords. Apical angle of about 30 °. Aperture missing.

children.name: Mesalia sovisi Harzhauser & Landau, 2019
children.description: Shell small, moderately slender to broad, of about 10 teleoconch whorls. Protoconch paucispiral comprising <two whorls with low, convex first whorl. Transition into teleoconch not well preserved in available material, indicated by onset of spiral sculpture of about 5 delicate spiral threads, which do not allow a separation into primary and secondary cords. Early teleoconch whorls slightly angulated in mid-whorl or regularly convex. Later whorls convex; periphery slightly below mid-whorl, occasionally coinciding with faint angulation; another faint angulation may appear slightly below adapical suture. Suture moderately incised. Sculpture of late teleoconch whorls consisting of numerous spiral cords with rounded-flat tops (about 30 – 35 on last whorl) separated by narrower interspaces, which may bear delicate secondary threads. Lateral sinus with low angle; wide, moderately deep, simple concave with faintly sigmoidal part close below adapical suture; maximum depth in adapical half of whorl. Basal sinus very shallow, weakly prosocyrt. Spiral sculpture persists on moderately convex base. Aperture subcircular, slightly effusive abapically; outer lip thin. Columella strongly concave, inner lip solid, narrowly reflected. Delicate, oblique fold rarely developed on adapical part of inner lip. No inner lirae developed. Shell measurements and ratios. Complete specimens (n = 5): SL = 21.3 mm (σ = 0.8 mm), MD: 7.2 mm (σ = 0.3 mm); AA: μ = 26.8 ° (σ = 1.1 °), PA: μ = 23.6 ° (σ = 0.6 °).

children.name: Mesalia styriaca Harzhauser & Landau, 2019
children.description: Shell small, moderately slender turriculate, of 13 teleoconch whorls. Protoconch paucispiral of about 1.5 smooth whorls with large nucleus; protoconch diameter ~ 600 μm; terminal protoconch whorl slightly angulated below mid-whorl. Early teleoconch whorls keeled, coinciding with rounded B spiral cord; sutural ramp flat to weakly concave. Keel starts close above abapical suture on early teleoconch whorls and moves towards midwhorl during ontogeny, passing into less prominent angulation on last whorls. Faint C and d spiral cords may appear. Entire shell covered by delicate spiral threads, covering also spiral cords. Lateral sinus angle low to moderately steep, ranging around 11 °; shallow, simple concave passing via weakly prosocyrt sinus into basal sinus; distinctly adapical LS p. Base rapidly contracting, covered by delicate spiral threads; basal sinus nearly straight to faintly prosocyrt. Aperture oblique ovate; basal lip slightly effusive, inner lip broad, reflected with distinct umbilical chink. Parietal callus thin, not expanding. No inner lirae developed. Shell measurements and ratios. Complete specimens are rare; based on the largest nearly complete specimens (Holotype, Paratype 1) the maximum SL ranges around 33.5 mm, maximum MD = 8.5 mm. n = 8 specimens: AA: μ = 20.0 ° (σ = 2.33 °), PA: μ = 14.8 ° (σ = 0.90 °). Lateral sinus (n = 6): LS angle = 11.0 ° (σ = 1.3 °), LS p = 0.7 (σ = 0.14), LS d = 7.1 (σ = 1.5).

children.name: Archimediella carpathica Harzhauser & Landau, 2019
children.description: Shell medium-sized, slender, comprising up to 20 teleoconch whorls. Protoconch moderately high, consisting of less than two strongly convex whorls with bulbous initial part; diameter 290 μm. Transition into teleoconch marked by onset of keel-like B spiral cord and slightly weaker C spiral cord. Both primary spiral cords persist throughout ontogeny forming two moderately raised cords with convex tops, separated by flat to weakly concave interspace. Sutural ramp indistinct, flat to feebly convex on late whorls. Weakly raised A spiral cord may develop on sutural ramp, typically accompanied adapically by two secondary spiral cords and one abapical one. Weaker tertiary spiral cords may appear in interspaces. Three tertiary spiral cords below C primary cord. Suture moderately to distinctly incised; whorl profile shifting from weakly convex to moderately frustate during ontogeny. Lateral sinus with moderately steep angle, ranging around 18.5 °; moderately deep with weak adapical inflection point; occasionally, weak abapical inflection point appears close to suture; abapical LS p. Basal sinus weakly opisthocyrt to slightly sigmoidal. Aperture semicircular; columella concave; parietal callus glossy, thin, weakly expanding. Base moderately convex with about five to eight wide-spaced spiral cords and intercalated secondary cords of variable strength.

children.name: Ptychidia erynella Harzhauser & Landau, 2019
children.description: Shell medium-sized, slender, of about 18 teleoconch whorls. Protoconch unknown. Early teleoconch whorls high, angulated at mid-whorl with deep suture. Onset of primaries not preserved; angulation coinciding with B spiral cord adjoined by weaker C spiral cord and faint A spiral cord (not always visible) starting at least on 3 rd to 4 th teleoconch whorls. Height of whorls successively decreasing ¸ angulation shifting slightly below mid-whorl on neanic whorls. B spiral cord most prominent, ranging from keel-like to convex. C spiral cord shifting down, close to suture, resulting in broad, convex interspace between B and C spiral cords. Sutural ramp flat to weakly convex with distinct A spiral cord, often accompanied by r cord and one or two tertiary spiral cords. Secondary spiral cord between B and C spiral cords, rarely equaling primaries; no additional secondary cords below C spiral cord aside from peribasal cord of variable strength. Lateral sinus simple, steep, maximum depth below mid-whorl, adapical part moderately convex without inflection point, abapical part weakly convex, nearly straight. Aperture subquadratic, higher than broad; outer lip thin, inner lip narrowly reflected firming narrow umbilical chink. Parietal callus glossy, thin, indistinct, covering only small part of base. Basal sinus nearly straight. Base moderately convex with about eight narrow, usually poorly developed, secondary spiral cords. No inner lirae detected in Austrian and French specimens.
